question:
What will come in place of 'A' in the given equation?

(A)/(192) = (48)/(A)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cross-multiply to isolate A² directly:

A² = 192 × 48

Break 192 into 4 × 48 to easily pair the values:

A = √(4 × 48 × 48) = 2 × 48 = 96

**∴ The correct answer is 96.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A / 192 = 48 / A

**Calculation:**

By cross-multiplying the terms on both sides:

⇒ A × A = 192 × 48

⇒ A² = (48 × 4) × 48

⇒ A² = 48² × 4

Taking the square root on both sides:

⇒ A = √(48² × 2²)

⇒ A = 48 × 2

⇒ A = 96

**∴ The correct answer is 96.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cross-Multiplication

When solving linear equations with equivalent fractions on both sides, cross-multiplying (multiplying the numerator of one side by the denominator of the other) directly yields an integer equation: a/b = c/d ⇒ a × d = b × c.

Simplifying Square Roots

Instead of multiplying large numbers to evaluate a perfect square, breaking the values down into prime factors and creating equivalent pairs helps calculate the root considerably faster. Using the property √(x² × y²) = x × y.
